haiku-low.q1: It doesn't differ: both return HTTP 401 with "Invalid email or password" and record a failure the same way. Unknown emails still run a bcrypt comparison against a dummy hash.
haiku-low.q2: The server returns HTTP 429 without looking up the user or checking the password. Failed attempts during the lock are not recorded.
haiku-low.q3: If the request carried a sid cookie, the old session is deleted in the same transaction that creates the new session.
haiku-low.q4: Only a random opaque session ID, with no user data. Flags are HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax; Path=/, so page scripts cannot read it.
haiku-low.q5: It stops 12 hours after creation, since that absolute limit can't be extended. The 30-minute idle limit doesn't apply while the user stays active.
haiku-low.q6: It treats the request as not signed in: the app clears the sid cookie and redirects with 302 to /login.
haiku-low.q7: The server deletes the session row, then clears the cookie and redirects 303 to /login. A missing session is a no-op with the same result.
haiku-low.q8: Sessions are rows in the shared Postgres database, so both instances see them. Any instance finds the session by looking up the cookie's SHA-256 hash.
haiku-low.q9: In the login_failures table, one row per failed attempt with email and failed_at. The server counts rows from the last 10 minutes by comparing failed_at to Postgres now().
haiku-low.q10: It compares the SHA-256 of the cookie against sessions, requiring last_seen_at within 30 minutes and created_at within 12 hours. When valid, it writes last_seen_at = now().
haiku-low.q11: The browser receives HTTP 503 with the plain page "Sign-in is temporarily unavailable. Please try again." The failure is not counted as a bad attempt.
haiku-low.q12: A cleanup job every 10 minutes on each instance deletes sessions past either limit, plus old failure rows and expired locks. Expired sessions are already rejected by the query.

sonnet.q1: They don't differ in the response: both return HTTP 401 with the login page showing "Invalid email or password", and both record a failure the same way (a dummy bcrypt compare is run for unknown emails).
sonnet.q2: The email is locked (a login_locks row, locked_until = now() + 15 min). POST /login returns HTTP 429 without looking up the user or checking the password, and failed attempts during the lock are not recorded.
sonnet.q3: The app deletes the old session in the same transaction that creates the new session (new random ID), then responds 303 to /dashboard with the new sid cookie.
sonnet.q4: Only a random opaque session ID (32 bytes, base64url); no user data. Page scripts cannot read it because it is HttpOnly (also Secure; SameSite=Lax; Path=/).
sonnet.q5: At 12 hours after login (absolute limit based on created_at, which never changes), even with continuous activity; the 30-minute idle limit keeps being renewed.
sonnet.q6: The UPDATE returns no row, so the app responds 302 to /login and clears the sid cookie (empty value, Max-Age=0).
sonnet.q7: The server deletes the session row by id_hash (a no-op if none exists), then clears the cookie and redirects (303) to /login. The result is the same whether or not a session existed.
sonnet.q8: In the sessions table in the shared Postgres database. Either instance hashes the cookie value with SHA-256 and looks up the row by id_hash (primary key).
sonnet.q9: In the login_failures table (email, failed_at; indexed on email, failed_at). The server counts that email's rows with failed_at within the last 10 minutes (sliding window), using Postgres now() as the time source.
sonnet.q10: It compares last_seen_at against now() minus 30 minutes (idle) and created_at against now() minus 12 hours (absolute), in one atomic UPDATE keyed on id_hash. If valid, it sets last_seen_at = now() and returns user_id.
sonnet.q11: NOT STATED for this exact case beyond the general rule: any DB failure fails closed with HTTP 503 and the page "Sign-in is temporarily unavailable. Please try again." The login failure is not counted as a bad attempt.
sonnet.q12: A cleanup job running every 10 minutes on each instance deletes sessions past the idle or absolute limit (also old login_failures and expired login_locks).
